Define a population pharmacokinetic model

Source: R/model.R
pk_model.Rd

Describes the structural model, the parameters with between-subject variability, the residual error and covariate effects. Nothing is compiled: the structure selects one of the precompiled closed-form models.

Usage

pk_model(
  structure = c("1cmt", "2cmt"),
  route = c("iv", "oral"),
  iiv = NULL,
  error = c("proportional", "additive", "combined", "log"),
  covariates = list(),
  correlated = FALSE,
  ka_faster = FALSE
)

Arguments

structure

"1cmt" or "2cmt".

route

"iv" (bolus, or infusion when the data have RATE > 0) or "oral" (first-order absorption).

iiv

Character vector of parameters with log-normal between-subject variability.

error

Residual error: "additive", "proportional", "combined" or "log" (additive on the log scale; DV must be positive).

covariates

A list of formulas, one or more per parameter, such as CL ~ (WT / 70)^0.75 (fixed exponent), CL ~ (WT / 70)^b_wt (estimated exponent named b_wt), CL ~ exp(b_age * (AGE - 40)) (estimated) or CL ~ (SEX == 1)^b_sex (estimated effect of a category). Terms can be multiplied: CL ~ (WT / 70)^0.75 * (CRCL / 100)^b_crcl.

correlated

Logical; estimate correlations between the random effects.

ka_faster

Logical, oral models only. If TRUE, the typical KA is constrained to be larger than the typical disposition rate (k = CL/V for 1-cmt, the fast rate alpha for 2-cmt) of a subject at the covariate reference values. This removes the flip-flop mode in which KA and the disposition rate swap. Use it only when absorption is known to be faster than distribution; it is wrong for flip-flop drugs such as many extended-release forms. The prior density on KA is kept and set to zero for KA <= rate (not renormalised). Default FALSE.

Value

An object of class bpk_model.

Details

Parameters are CL, V (1-compartment) or CL, V1, Q, V2 (2-compartment), plus KA for oral absorption. For oral dosing, bioavailability is not estimated, so CL, V, Q and V2 are apparent values (divided by F).

Examples

pk_model("2cmt", route = "oral", iiv = c("CL", "V1", "KA"),
         covariates = list(CL ~ (WT / 70)^0.75))
#> bayespk model: 2cmt oral 
#>   parameters: CL, V1, Q, V2, KA 
#>   between-subject variability (log-normal): CL, V1, KA  
#>   residual error: proportional 
#>   covariates:
#>     CL ~ (WT/70)^0.75
